hero.headline: You're scaling up while the whole world is changing.
hero.sub: AI alone won't get you there. An aligned leadership team will.
hero.body: Your company is growing fast, and AI is changing how work gets done at the same time. Your leaders are carrying both. A one-off coaching session or an annual offsite won't hold up under that.
hero.body2: Human First AI stays with your leaders every day: short, regular check-ins. An AI guide built on decades of leadership coaching. A library of 3–5 minute micro-courses in audio and article form. And peer groups where leaders solve real problems together and build trust while doing it — resulting in faster execution, better decisions, and stronger business performance.

pov.headline: Leadership is the difference between buying AI and getting value from it.
pov.body1: Every growth-stage company is investing in AI. Far fewer are seeing the return they expected. The gap is rarely the technology. It comes down to whether leaders can make clear decisions, set priorities people understand, and help their teams actually change how they work.
pov.body2: As you scale, every leader touches more decisions, more people, and more change. Strategy and tools create the opportunity. Leaders decide whether it turns into results.
pov.body3: The companies that pull ahead won't be the ones that spend the most on AI. They'll be the ones whose leaders turn adoption into real output, week after week.

box1.img: Photo placeholder — Elena in a leadership meeting with her executive team
box1.body: Elena, CEO of a 200-person logistics scale-up, is driving an ambitious AI transformation. She hands the rollout to her six-person executive team, each leading their own senior leaders and expected to turn strategy into results across their part of the business.

box2.img: Photo placeholder — Friction in a team rollout meeting
box2.body: Within weeks, cracks appear everywhere at once. Teams resist new tools, accountability slips, and once-decisive leaders go quiet in meetings while timelines slip across departments. What was meant to be Elena's competitive advantage starts looking like the thing most likely to break the company from the inside.

box3.img: Photo placeholder — Elena and a coach reviewing the leadership programme
box3.body: Elena had already invested in a leadership programme. The principles were right and the content was strong. But a two-day workshop doesn't survive the first hard Tuesday six weeks later. She brings in Human First AI not to replace that investment, but to keep its momentum alive in the moments the workshop can't reach.

box4.img: Photo placeholder — A leader starting the morning with the app
box4.intro: Human First AI becomes part of the day, not a programme to remember. A two-minute check-in, coaching from Eve before a difficult conversation, a Micro-course on the commute, and a Think Tank that holds them to what they committed. Small daily habits that compound into how they actually lead.

box5.img: Photo placeholder — The executive team in a high-energy, productive session
box5.body: Within weeks, the shift is visible. Leaders who'd gone quiet start making decisions again and teams regain a clear sense of ownership. Elena sees firsthand that surviving an AI transformation was never about the tools. It was about whether her leaders could stay steady enough to lead through it.

product.headline: Five connected pieces. One habit: follow through.

pillar1.title: Daily Check-in
pillar1.body: Accountability starts with yourself. A two-minute pulse on mood, energy, sleep, and stress. Over time, the patterns show leaders how they're really doing before it shows up in how they lead.

pillar2.title: Ask Eve
pillar2.body: An AI guide trained on decades of coaching experience. When a leader faces a hard decision, uncertainty, or a difficult conversation, Eve helps them think it through, choose a course, and stay accountable to the commitments they make.

pillar3.title: Micro-learning
pillar3.body: The right skill, at the moment it's needed. 3–5 minute courses in audio and article form, matched to what a leader is dealing with right now. Small enough to fit a workday. Regular enough to become a habit.

pillar4.title: Think Tanks
pillar4.body: Peers who hold you to it. Small groups of leaders working through similar challenges. A trusted space to solve problems together and hold each other to what was agreed.

pillar5.title: Real-time Data
pillar5.body: For founders and execs: know how your leadership team is doing daily, not every 6 months. Aggregated, anonymised signals show where energy is high, where stress is building, and which teams need support — early enough to step in.

step1.title: Build resilient leaders
step1.body: Daily practice gives leaders the habits and confidence to keep leading well through constant change.
